summary: Objectives gain native numeric bad-event ratios, honest covered-time gauges, explicit budget policies and fleet-owned bindings to built-in rows. The TypeScript DSL lowers these declarations to the same strict KDL reader used by the kernel.

replay.detail: Existing interval and count declarations retain their semantics. New budget evidence does not fabricate history before a source begins observing.

schema.detail: Objective declarations accept ratio, gauge and native indicators and optional budget policies. Ratio events name their numeric field, threshold and timestamp. Gauges additionally declare cadence, maximum sample age and an upper or lower threshold. Policies declare allowance, horizon, minimum coverage and samples, and paired fast/slow burn windows.

rules.detail: Bad-event fractions and bad covered duration spend their declared allowance. Gauge gaps remain unknown; effective burn windows expand to at least one cadence short and two cadences long. Native owner bindings inherit source policy without allowing overrides.

compatibility.detail: Existing objective syntax remains valid. No client or peer transport schema change is required by the declaration extensions; public built-in definitions contain no private fleet owner IDs.

downtime.detail: No data conversion or planned downtime.

manual.detail: Optionally declare a namespaced native binding with on-breach to assign a fleet owner to a built-in row. New ratio/gauge objectives require an explicit budget policy; native bindings inherit it.

recovery.detail: Remove or correct an invalid declaration through the normal declaration workflow; no recovery payload or backfill is introduced.
